answer: Each identity must finish a sequential delay puzzle bound to its own key before it can trade: every step feeds the next, so adding cores does not help, and one puzzle takes about 6 hours of single-thread CPU. Peers verify the finished chain in seconds, like light through a prism splitting one claim into checkable parts, and only then does the identity step onto the trading ledge. A glacier pace is the point: 100 fake identities cost 600 CPU-hours, no bulk discount, so a sybil farm pays linearly for every fake it fields.
